question: A dealer purchased an oven for ₹54,000. He allows a discount of 10% on its marked price and still gains 75%. Find the marked price of the oven.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Marked Price (MP)** to **Cost Price (CP)** is given by: **MP/CP = (100 + Gain%) / (100 − Discount%)**.

Substituting the values: MP / 54,000 = (100 + 75) / (100 − 10).

MP / 54,000 = 175 / 90.

MP = 54,000 × (175 ÷ 90) = 600 × 175.

MP = 1,05,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,05,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: **Cost Price (CP)** = ₹54,000, **Gain%** = 75%, **Discount%** = 10%.

Formulas: **Selling Price (SP)** = CP × (100 + Gain%) ÷ 100 | **Marked Price (MP)** = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 − Discount%).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c5233688a68e779fe06e292fec2982204a7d36b6ea8bce3f5794dec4ae9d9d78.png] 

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 54,000 × (175 ÷ 100) = 54,000 × 1.75 = ₹94,500.

⇒ Let **Marked Price** be MP. SP = MP × (100 − 10) ÷ 100 = 0.9 × MP.

⇒ 94,500 = 0.9 × MP.

⇒ MP = 94,500 ÷ 0.9 = ₹1,05,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,05,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**. SP = MP − Discount.

Relation between CP and MP

The direct formula **CP/MP = (100 − D%) / (100 + G%)** is very useful for competitive exams to save time.
